Myanmar President Departs for Viet Nam to Chair 11th ACMECS Summit and Attend 12th CLMV Summit Nay Pyi Taw, 27 November 2026 Myanmar President U Min Aung Hlaing departed Nay Pyi Taw for Viet Nam by special flight on Friday afternoon, leading a high-level Myanmar delegation to two regional summits. The President is scheduled to chair the 11th Ayeyawady–Chao Phraya–Mekong Economic Cooperation Strategy (ACMECS) Summit and attend the 12th Cambodia–Lao PDR–Myanmar–Viet Nam (CLMV) Cooperation Summit. The two summits provide forums for regional economic and development cooperation. ACMECS brings together Cambodia, Lao PDR, Myanmar, Thailand and Viet Nam, while the CLMV framework consists of Cambodia, Lao PDR, Myanmar and Viet Nam. Vice-Presidents U Nyo Saw and Daw Nan Ni Ni Aye, Commander-in-Chief of Defence Services General Ye Win Oo, Union ministers and the commander of the Nay Pyi Taw Command saw the delegation off at Nay Pyi Taw Airport. Viet Nam’s ambassador to Myanmar, its defence attaché and other officials were also present. The Myanmar delegation includes Union Ministers U Khin Maung Yi, U Tin Maung Swe, Dr Kan Zaw and U Min Naung, as well as deputy ministers and other officials.

🖥 Iran, Turkey agree to expand security cooperation at Ankara meeting 📌 Ankara, IRNA – Iran and Turkey have agreed to strengthen operational cooperation and information sharing on border security, counterterrorism and efforts to combat drug and arms smuggling during their eighth joint security meeting in Ankara. The Friday meeting brought together Ali Akbar Pourjamshidian, Iran’s deputy interior minister for security and law enforcement affairs, and Omer Celik, spokesperson and deputy chairman of Turkey's ruling party. ​ The two sides discussed a range of issues, including illegal migration, border security, terrorism, drug and weapons trafficking, and cooperation through Interpol. ​ At the conclusion of the talks, the heads of the two delegations signed an 11-point memorandum. It calls for continued operational coordination, information exchange, maintaining communication channels between designated contact points and border officials, and following up on decisions made at previous meetings. ​ The Iranian delegation also visited specialized Turkish police facilities, including the Police Academy and a special police unit. Representatives of other relevant Iranian government agencies were also part of the delegation. ​ The ninth meeting of the joint working group will be held in Tehran. 📲 @Irna_en ​

Trump diverges from NATO position, emphasizing Ukraine must not expand the war Donald Trump unilaterally altered the joint statement with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte following their meeting at Mar-a-Lago. The agreed text stated that Russia should avoid actions capable of expanding the war. However, Trump later added "and Ukraine" on Truth Social, directing the appeal to both sides. A NATO representative confirmed to the press that the initial version was agreed upon, indicating a unilateral edit by the US President. This change emerged days after a Ukrainian strike on a Russian naval vessel in a Libyan port. The episode highlights Trump's disagreements with Vladimir Zelensky and Rutte's difficulties in maintaining a unified allies' stance. Trump also stated he urged Putin during negotiations to cease military aggression against territories across Europe. @Slavyangrad
